posts.title: Teen Patti Gold Old Version: Why Players Search for It
posts.excerpt: Teen Patti Gold old version is searched by players who miss a feature, bonus, or interface from an earlier release. Here is what changed, and the real risks of downloading old APKs.
posts.author: AllYonoGuru Team
posts.content:
Teen Patti Gold is one of the most widely played Teen Patti apps in India. When a major update changes the interface, removes a feature, or adjusts the free chips system, a significant number of players immediately search for the old version. If you are one of them, this guide is worth reading before you download anything from a third-party site.

## Why Players Search for Teen Patti Gold Old Version

The most common reasons players want an older version of Teen Patti Gold:

**Free chips system changed.** Teen Patti Gold's daily free chip bonuses have been revised multiple times. Players who remember receiving larger daily bonuses in earlier versions sometimes search for those versions hoping to access the old bonus amounts — not realising that bonus structures are server-side and not version-dependent.

**Interface was redesigned.** Teen Patti Gold has gone through multiple UI overhauls. Players comfortable with a previous layout sometimes find the new one disorienting and want to return to familiar navigation.

**A favourite game variant was modified or moved.** The app has added and repositioned variants over the years. A variant that was prominent in a previous version may still exist but be accessed differently in the current one.

**Performance issues on older devices.** As apps grow more feature-rich, they become heavier. Players on older or budget Android phones sometimes find earlier versions ran faster with less battery drain.

## What Has Changed Across Major Versions

Teen Patti Gold major updates have typically included:

- Addition of new variants (Joker, Muflis, AK47, and others added at different points)
- Revised free chip refresh intervals and amounts
- New tournament formats and leaderboard systems
- Updated minimum buy-in requirements for certain tables
- Security updates and anti-cheat improvements
- Significant UI redesigns affecting navigation and table lobby layout

The current version generally has more content and better security than any previous version, even if the interface feels less familiar initially.

## The Risk of Downloading an Old APK

**Third-party APK sites are not verified by the developer.** Teen Patti Gold is developed by Octro. Old versions are not officially distributed anywhere — any APK on a third-party site claiming to be an old version has not been checked by Octro and may contain modified code, adware, or data collection tools beyond what the official app includes.

**Chip and account balances are server-side.** Your chip count lives on Octro's servers, not on your device. Reverting to an old APK does not restore old bonus amounts or chip counts — your account state is exactly as the server holds it regardless of which version you run.

**Old versions may be locked out.** Octro, like most developers, enforces minimum version requirements. An APK older than the minimum supported version will either fail to connect or immediately prompt a forced update.

**Free chips are the same regardless of version.** If the daily bonus changed in a recent update, that change is in the server configuration — not in the app file itself. Running an older APK will not give you the older bonus amounts.

## What to Do Instead

If the interface changed: spend 15 minutes exploring the current version's menus. Most UI changes in Teen Patti Gold are navigational rather than feature removals — the same content is usually still there, just reorganised.

If performance is the issue: clear the app cache (Settings → Apps → Teen Patti Gold → Clear Cache), ensure at least 1GB of free storage is available, and restart your device.

If you miss a variant: check the full variant list in the current lobby — variants are often accessible from a secondary filter or a dedicated section that new players sometimes miss.

For a complete guide to Teen Patti rules across all variants available in the app, see our [3 Patti rules guide](/blog/3-patti-rules-complete-guide). For Muflis specifically — one of the variants that has changed placement across versions — see our [Muflis Teen Patti guide](/blog/muflis-teen-patti-rules). For other Teen Patti apps in our directory, see [Teen Patti Guru](/teen-patti-guru).

---

### Where can I download Teen Patti Gold old version?

Octro does not officially distribute old versions. Any third-party source offering old APKs is unverified and potentially unsafe. The safest option is the current version from Octro's official website or the Google Play Store.

### Will an old version give me more free chips?

No. Free chip amounts are set server-side, not in the app file. Running an older APK will not restore previous bonus amounts — your account receives whatever the current server configuration provides.

### Is Teen Patti Gold available on the Play Store?

Yes — Teen Patti Gold by Octro is available on the Google Play Store for the play-money (non-real-money) version. Real-money variants may require a separate APK download depending on your region.

### What changed in recent Teen Patti Gold updates?

Recent updates have included new variants, revised tournament formats, UI changes, and security improvements. Check the update notes in the Play Store listing or on Octro's official website for version-specific details.

posts.title: Rummy Points Calculation: How Scores Are Counted
posts.excerpt: In 13-card rummy every ungrouped card in your hand costs you points when another player declares. Here is exactly how points are counted, what the cap is, and how scoring affects different formats.
posts.author: AllYonoGuru Team
posts.content:
Understanding how points are calculated in 13-card rummy is essential before you play at any real-money table. Points determine how much you pay when you lose a hand, and knowing the point value of every card in your hand at any moment lets you make smarter decisions about when to drop, what to discard, and when to declare.

## Point Values for Every Card

In standard 13-card Indian Rummy, point values are fixed:

- **Ace (A)** — 10 points
- **King (K)** — 10 points
- **Queen (Q)** — 10 points
- **Jack (J)** — 10 points
- **10** — 10 points
- **9** — 9 points
- **8** — 8 points
- **7** — 7 points
- **6** — 6 points
- **5** — 5 points
- **4** — 4 points
- **3** — 3 points
- **2** — 2 points
- **Joker (printed or wild)** — 0 points

Only **ungrouped cards** contribute to your penalty score. Cards that are part of a valid sequence or set count as zero, regardless of their face value.

## How Penalty Points Are Calculated

When another player makes a valid declaration, everyone else's hand is evaluated. For each player who has not declared:

1. Valid groupings (sequences and sets) are identified and removed from the count.
2. The face values of all remaining ungrouped cards are added together.
3. This total is the player's penalty score for that round.

**Example:** Your hand at the moment another player declares contains: a valid pure sequence (7♠-8♠-9♠), an impure sequence with a joker (4♥-Joker-6♥), and ungrouped cards K♦, Q♣, 3♥. Your penalty = 10 + 10 + 3 = 23 points.

## The Maximum Penalty Cap

Most Indian rummy platforms cap the maximum penalty at **80 points** per hand. This means even if your ungrouped cards total 120 points, you are charged only 80.

The cap protects players from catastrophic single-hand losses in Points Rummy, where penalties are multiplied by the point value per rupee. At ₹5 per point, an 80-point loss costs ₹400 — painful, but not ruinous.

## Invalid Declaration Penalty

If you declare incorrectly — pressing the declare button without a valid hand — the penalty is typically the maximum (80 points) regardless of your actual card count. This is one of the most costly mistakes in the game, and it is why experienced players verify their hand structure carefully before declaring.

A valid hand requires:
- At least one pure sequence (no jokers)
- At least one more sequence (can be impure)
- Remaining cards in valid sets or sequences

For a full breakdown of what makes a valid hand, see our [rummy sequence rules guide](/blog/rummy-sequence-rules-pure-sequence-explained).

## How Points Translate to Money

In Points Rummy, each point has a rupee value agreed before the game starts. The winner collects the sum of all other players' penalty points multiplied by the point value.

**Example:** 6-player Points Rummy at ₹2 per point. Five players lose with penalties of 25, 40, 55, 70, and 80 points. Total: 270 points. The winner earns 270 × ₹2 = ₹540 (minus platform rake).

In Pool Rummy, points accumulate across rounds toward an elimination threshold (101 or 201). The point value per rupee concept does not apply — the fixed entry fee is what's at stake. See our [pool rummy rules guide](/blog/pool-rummy-rules-points-pool-deals) for how Pool scoring works.

## Practical Implications for Play

**Count your ungrouped points before deciding to drop.** If your ungrouped cards total less than 20 points, staying in may be worth it — a first drop costs 20 points. If they total more than 40 points and the hand is going badly, a middle drop at 40 points saves you from a larger loss.

**Discard high-value ungrouped cards early.** Holding an unconnected King, Queen, and Jack is 30 points of potential penalty. Discard them in turns 1–3 if they are not part of any forming sequence. See our [rummy discard strategy guide](/blog/rummy-discard-strategy) for full guidance.

**Track opponents' potential declarations.** If a player at your table is drawing and discarding quickly with minimal reorganisation, they may be close to declaring. Count your ungrouped points and decide whether to accelerate your hand building or consider a strategic drop.

For apps where you can practice at low-stakes tables, see [Rummy Guru](/rummy-guru) and [All Rummy App](/all-rummy-app).

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How many points is an Ace in rummy?

An Ace counts as 10 points in 13-card Indian Rummy — the same as King, Queen, Jack, and 10. It is a high-value card to hold ungrouped.

### Do jokers have points in rummy?

No. Both printed jokers and wild jokers count as 0 points. An unused joker in your hand at the end of a round does not contribute to your penalty score.

### What is the maximum penalty in rummy?

Most platforms cap the maximum penalty at 80 points per hand, regardless of how many ungrouped points your cards actually total.

### How are points calculated in Pool Rummy?

In Pool Rummy, your penalty points from each round accumulate toward the elimination threshold (101 or 201). Once your cumulative total reaches or exceeds the threshold, you are eliminated from the game.

posts.title: Yono Arcade Games: What's Available and How They Work
posts.excerpt: Yono Arcade games are faster-paced Android apps that go beyond rummy and teen patti. Here is what arcade-format games in the Yono network offer, how they work, and what to check before playing.
posts.author: AllYonoGuru Team
posts.content:
Yono Arcade games refer to a category of Android apps in the Yono network that offer formats beyond traditional rummy and teen patti. If you have been looking for something faster-paced with shorter rounds and different mechanics, arcade-format games may be worth exploring — but they come with their own set of things to understand before you play.

## What Are Yono Arcade Games?

The term arcade in the Yono context covers several game types:

**Colour Prediction Games** — players predict which colour (red or green, or a numbered outcome) a timer will land on. Rounds are short — typically 30 seconds to 3 minutes. Entry amounts and payouts are fixed per the app's payout table.

**Crash Games** — a multiplier rises from 1x upward and can crash at any moment. Players must cash out before the crash. The longer you wait, the higher the potential multiplier — but if the crash comes first, you lose your stake.

**Aviator and Similar Formats** — a variant of crash games where a plane or similar visual element represents the rising multiplier. The mechanic is identical to crash games.

**Fast Card Games** — simplified card formats with shorter decision windows than full Teen Patti or Rummy. Some apps offer Dragon vs. Tiger (one card each, higher card wins) or Andar Bahar as arcade-speed formats.

**Mini-Games** — coin flips, dice rolls, and other single-decision formats that resolve instantly.

## How Arcade Games Differ From Rummy and Teen Patti

The key differences:

- **Speed** — arcade rounds resolve in seconds to minutes. A full Pool Rummy game can take 30+ minutes. Arcade formats are designed for rapid play.
- **Skill component** — rummy and teen patti have significant skill elements (hand building, opponent reading). Colour prediction and crash games have minimal skill components — timing and risk management are the only decisions.
- **Transparency** — rummy has clear hand rankings and deterministic outcomes. Arcade games use random number generators or server-side algorithms whose fairness is harder to verify independently.

## What to Check Before Playing Arcade Games

**Look for a provably fair or RNG certification.** Legitimate arcade-game apps display information about how their random number generator works. An app that cannot explain how outcomes are determined should not be trusted with real money.

**Understand the house edge.** Every arcade game has a mathematical advantage built in for the platform. Colour prediction games typically pay 1.9x on a winning bet (not 2x), which represents a 5% house edge. Check the exact payout multiplier before playing.

**Set very strict loss limits.** Arcade games move fast, which means losses accumulate faster than in card games. Set a session loss limit in rupees before you start and stop when you reach it — do not chase losses in a fast-paced format.

**Verify withdrawals before depositing.** The same rule applies here as for any Yono app — look for independent player reports of successful withdrawals before depositing on a new arcade-format app.

For arcade apps reviewed and listed in our directory, see our [Yono Games section](/yono-games). For a broader overview of what is new in the Yono network in 2026, see our [new Yono games guide](/blog/new-yono-games-2026). For the complete list of established Yono apps, see our [all Yono games list](/blog/all-yono-games-complete-list-android).

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What are Yono Arcade games?

Yono Arcade games are fast-paced Android apps in the Yono network that use formats like colour prediction, crash games, Aviator, and mini-card games. They offer shorter rounds than rummy or teen patti.

### Are Yono Arcade games skill-based?

Most arcade formats (colour prediction, crash, coin flip) have minimal skill components. Risk management and loss limit discipline matter, but outcomes are primarily determined by random number generators.

### How do you win at Yono Arcade games?

In crash games, cash out early (at lower multipliers) to win consistently smaller amounts — waiting for high multipliers increases both the potential reward and the risk of a crash before you exit. In colour prediction, no strategy changes the mathematical house edge.

### Are Yono Arcade apps on the Google Play Store?

No. Yono-network arcade apps distribute as direct APK downloads from developer websites, not through the Play Store.
